diagram.exampleGroups:
flowchart TD
  subgraph client [App]
    ui[Sign-in screen] --> api[Call API]
  end
  subgraph server [Server]
    auth{{Authentication}} --> db[(Database)]
  end
  api ==> auth
  db -.-> ui
diagram.exampleLeftRight:
flowchart LR
  idea[Idea] --> draft[Draft] --> review{Approved?}
  review -- no --> draft
  review -- yes --> delivery([Delivery])
diagram.exampleProcess:
flowchart TD
  A([Start]) --> B[Receive order]
  B --> C{Payment approved?}
  C -->|Yes| D[Pick items]
  C -->|No| E[Notify the customer]
  E --> B
  D --> F[(Stock)]
  D --> G([End])

diagramGuide.boxesNote: Format: alias[Box text]. The sign around the text sets the shape.
diagramGuide.comments: Lines starting with %% are ignored — use them for notes.
diagramGuide.intro: The idea is simple: each line of text describes one piece of the drawing. You give each box a short alias (no spaces, e.g. pay) and use that alias to connect the boxes with arrows. The text shown inside a box goes between brackets, parentheses or braces — and the kind of sign picks the box shape. Click Insert to put any example into your text.
diagramGuide.linksNote: Format: alias1 --> alias2. If a box doesn't exist yet, it's created with the alias itself as its text.
diagramGuide.readAloud: “Top to bottom: a capsule Order arrived leads to a diamond Is it paid?; if Yes, it goes to Pick items; if No, to Notify customer.”
diagramGuide.shortcuts: Shortcuts: a --> b --> c connects in sequence · a & b --> c connects two boxes to one · a -- No --> b is another way to put text on the arrow.
diagramGuide.subgraph: subgraph alias [Title] opens the group and end closes it. Everything in between stays inside the frame.
